You draw one hat or one pair of shades for Bottom Busters, a comedy pixel-art game, as a recipe of flat shapes. Code draws the recipe: every shape fills its region, a thick dark outline is added wherever a region meets empty space or another region, and the result is scaled up with hard pixel edges. No shading, no gradients, no text.

The grid:
- A hat is drawn on a grid 32 wide (x 0 to 32) and 30 tall (y 0 to 30), y going down. Its bottom edge (y about 28 to 30) is the brim, which sits on the head, so the hat must reach the bottom. Every character faces right, so anything that leans, flops or hangs goes to the left, the back of the head.
- Shades are drawn on a grid 24 wide and 9 tall: two lenses, one centered near x 5.5 and one near x 17.5, with a bridge between them around x 10 to 13. Each lens sits on an eye.

The recipe is one JSON object:
"name": the item's name
"kind": "hat" or "shades"
"regions": a list of {"id": a number, "name": a capitalized word, "color": [red, green, blue], "colorable": true or false}. A hat has 1 to 3 colorable regions, numbered 1, 2 and 3: the parts a player can recolor. Fixed parts are numbered 4 and up. Shades have no colorable regions; number their regions 5 and up.
"shapes": a list, drawn in order, later shapes over earlier ones. Each is one of:
  {"shape": "poly", "points": [[x, y], [x, y], [x, y], ...], "region": id}
  {"shape": "ellipse", "box": [left, top, right, bottom], "region": id}
  {"shape": "rect", "box": [left, top, right, bottom], "region": id}
  {"shape": "line", "points": [[x, y], [x, y]], "width": 1 to 6, "region": id}
  Region 0 erases.
"outline": leave it out for the usual dark outline, or give [red, green, blue] (the silver aviators' wire is silver).
Make the item read at a glance: one strong outline you'd know anywhere, big simple parts, every part at least 3 grid units across. Answer with only the JSON object.

## 21. Content guide

Every content agent reads the opening of this section, then its own part, before it generates anything. Rulings carry the Studio Director's name and date.

**The game, for every agent.** Bottom Busters is a comedy arcade game. Every character is a chubby man in white briefs who floats like a balloon and flies by farting. A character's health is two cheeks, and lives are white underwear icons. The humor is gross-out and physical. Poo piles up and dirties bodies, cheeks and hats, and the base coat never washes off. Other humor-first visuals include cheek "health" and the chef animals in the bonus rounds. Everything new has to read at game size and sit beside what's already in the game. Nothing is copied from real people, brands, logos, or characters from other games or shows.

### 21.3 Hats and shades (Wardrobe Stylist)

**What it is.** Wearables players put on at Character Select. The game has four today: the Santa hat, the turkey hat, black shades and silver aviators. Each item is drawn by code from flat shapes, the same way those four were (Studio Director, 2026-11-04).

**Style.**
- Pixel art on the characters' own grid.
- A thick dark outline all the way round.
- Flat fills, with no shading or gradients.
- It has to look like it belongs with the four already in the game.

**Color.**
- A hat has one to three color areas that players recolor at Character Select.
- Shades take no colors.

**Fit.**
- Every character faces right, so a hat leans or flops left, toward the back of the head.
- A hat's bottom edge is its brim, and it sits on the head.
- Shades have two lenses, one on each eye, with a bridge between them.
- Every item has to sit right on every character.

**Failure.**
- An item that doesn't read as what it is at game size, or reads as a blob.
- Off-style art.
- A hat that floats above the head, or shades that miss the eyes.
- Real logos, brands or team names.

End of the GDD extract.

(GDD: "It has to look like it belongs with the four already in the game."). Redesign the hat using simpler, more cartoonish flat shapes that match the existing hats' style—avoid tall, structured silhouettes. Ensure it sits correctly on the character’s head and maintains the same visual language as the current wearables.
